trust_decision.summary: The table name embedded in a client-supplied mysql:// resource URI is untrusted and must be neutralised before it is spliced into SQL; the decision is made in read_resource at src/mysql_mcp_server/server.py:87-95, where parts[0] is interpolated directly into SELECT * FROM {table} with no validation or quoting. The published fix neutralises that sink with a whitelist helper and backticks (and also guards the new USE `{db}` route).

landing_point.why: The advisory summary points at the mysql URI handler; read_resource is the only handler that turns part of a mysql:// URI into SQL, and this f-string is the interpolation site.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared validate_identifier helper, called from read_resource
MCP resource read: mysql://database/<name> (read_resource; the route itself is added by this same commit)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no other identifier sink at the pinned commit; the only other SQL sink, execute_sql (src/mysql_mcp_server/server.py:145), passes caller-supplied SQL by design, so a solver leaving it alone is correct, not scope-limited.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A table literally named `database` is readable at the pinned commit: list_resources advertises mysql://database/data (src/mysql_mcp_server/server.py:65) and read_resource selects that table (src/mysql_mcp_server/server.py:95). The fix's new `parts[0] == "database"` branch (fix.diff:450) redirects that same URI to USE `data`, so the real table becomes unreadable. Separately, the strict ^[a-zA-Z0-9_$]+$ whitelist (fix.diff:303) rejects legitimate MySQL identifiers that merely need backtick quoting (dash, dot, space, non-ASCII), even though quoting makes them safe.

O6_input_shapes: table identifier carried in the URI authority: mysql://<table>/data, taken as parts[0]
database identifier carried in the first path segment: mysql://database/<db>, taken as parts[1] (route added by the same fix)
both shapes normalised to the ^[a-zA-Z0-9_$]+$ whitelist and emitted backtick-quoted

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a qualified read route such as mysql://<db>/<table>/data that interpolates two identifiers into USE/SELECT
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the published fix itself adds exactly this shape of database route (fix.diff:450-455), so a maintainer adding multi-database support beside the same sink is natural

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a list_resources variant that filters on a caller-supplied database name, building SHOW TABLES FROM {db}
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: multi-database mode (added by the same commit) needs a database selector, and the neighbouring sink already interpolates an identifier unquoted

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a convenience table-preview tool that builds SELECT * FROM {table} from a tool argument
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: execute_sql already takes a free-form argument and the project advertises controlled table exploration, so a helper tool next to it is plausible

O9_family: SQL injection (CWE-74; identifier interpolated into SQL without neutralisation)

services: MySQL server: tests use a mysql:8.0 service container (.github/workflows/test.yml:14-22) and the server connects to MYSQL_HOST at runtime
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_server.py has four non-DB tests at the pinned commit (server init, list_tools, invalid tool name, missing query) plus one MySQL-gated list_resources test, and no test covers read_resource or identifier validation; tests/conftest.py builds a session MySQL fixture.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bind the table name as a parameter (cursor.execute('SELECT * FROM %s LIMIT 100', (table,))) or escape quotes; MySQL renders that as a string literal and the query breaks, and neither approach addresses the authority/path parse that supplies the identifier.

out_of_scope_notes: The published fix commit 080bef9 bundles the security change with unrelated 0.3.0 feature work (optional MYSQL_DATABASE/multi-database mode, SSE transport, SSL options, NULL/error rendering), which is why the diff has six source hunks; only the read_resource hunks close this advisory.
The GHSA prose was not available offline; the vulnerability description is inferred from the supplied summary and the fix diff.
unverified: Exact repository size in MB (no shell access); the tree has four Python files (server.py is 202 lines), so tiny_repo is asserted from the file listing rather than a measured byte count.

Whether pydantic AnyUrl (src/mysql_mcp_server/server.py:78-81) preserves or percent-encodes/ lowercases candidate payload characters before str(uri) is split was not checked by running code; no project code was executed.
The O5 `table named database` collision and the over-strict-whitelist breakage are code-reading inferences, not exercised against a live MySQL.
Advisory write-up breadth was not researched beyond the supplied IDs, so O13 is an estimate.
